claim: Players with equal scores appear in sign-up order, and ranks skip after a tie, so two players tied for first are followed by rank 3.
why: sorted with reverse=True still keeps equal items in their original order, so ties stay in sign-up order. The rank of a row is copied from the row above on a tie and otherwise is its position, giving 1, 1, 3, 3, 5. The trap is the belief that reverse=True flips tied items too.

deciding.note: reverse=True keeps ties in original order

root.claim: Ties keep sign-up order and ranks go 1, 1, 3.

atoms.claim: Equal-score players appear in sign-up order
atoms.evidence: main.py prints lee then ned (both 70) and kim then moe (both 50), the roster order; sorted(reverse=True) is stable.

atoms.claim: After two players tied at rank 1 the next rank is 3
